import Mathlib

/- Three prime numbers $p, q$, and $r$, greater than 3, form an arithmetic progression: $q=p+d, r=p+2 d$. Prove that $d$ is divisible by 6.

# -/
theorem number_theory_235644 (p q r d : ℕ) (hpqr : p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ r.Prime)
    (hqr : q = p + d) (hrr : r = p + 2 * d) (h1 : p > 3) (h2 : q > 3) (h3 : r > 3) :
    6 ∣ d := by

  have h8 : d % 2 = 0 := by

        all_goals try linarith

          linarith [eq1, h_eq0]
        contradiction
      -- From 4 / y = 1 / y and y ≠ 0, we can derive a contradiction
      have eq3 : 4 = 1 := by
        field_simp [h_eq6] at eq2 ⊢
        all_goals linarith
      linarith
    have h3 : y ≠ 0 := by
      by_contra h4
      have eq4 : y = 0 := h4
      have eq5 : x + y = x := by 
        linarith [eq4]
      have eq6 : x ≠ 0 := by

        contradiction
      have eq3 : 4 / x = 1 / x := by

        norm_num at h ⊢
        all_goals try linarith
      have eq4 : 4 = 1 := by
        field_simp [eq6] at eq3 ⊢
        all_goals linarith
